transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with severe depression and a constant feeling of emptiness for about two years now. It has become incredibly hard for me to function or do anything in my daily life. I just really need help dealing with this constant low mood.
During these past two years, have there been any periods of a few months or longer where your mood lifted and you felt mostly like yourself, or has this low mood been present almost every single day?

The constant low mood hasn't actually been there for the whole two years, but just for the last eight months. Before that, there were periods where my mood felt much lighter and more normal. Even during those times, though, I was still dealing with other things like hearing voices and having strange thoughts.
Can you tell me if you have experienced these voices or strange thoughts during times when your mood was normal, or do they only happen when you are feeling depressed?

Yes, I've definitely experienced them even when my mood felt completely normal. There was actually a period of about two weeks where I didn't feel depressed at all, but the voices and strange thoughts were still happening.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were [Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type), Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features]. The patient's report that psychotic symptoms (voices and strange thoughts) persisted for a period of two weeks during which their mood was 'completely normal' makes Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features unlikely, as that diagnosis requires psychotic symptoms to occur exclusively during episodes of major depression. The presence of psychotic symptoms in the absence of a mood episode for at least two weeks, in the context of a depressive episode, supports the diagnosis of Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type).
